title: too-far-future date scenario given {MOVE_IN_DATE} (today+90d) — the validation error it exists to pin can never fire
evidence: Scenario: `expected_outcome: validation_error` / `expected_error_fields:` / `  - desired_move_in_date` / `  desired_move_in_date: "{MOVE_IN_DATE}"`. SKILL.md:279: `Only the boundary-validation scenarios (`desired-move-in-date-in-past`, `-too-far-future`) pin literal dates on purpose.` Server rule (application_handler.gleam:1137-1139): `case calendar.naive_date_compare(candidate, move_in_limit(today)) {` / `order.Gt -> Error("Pick a date within the next year.")` with move_in_limit = today + 12 months. Scenario description still says: `bump `desired_move_in_date` further out so this scenario keeps` (referring to the deleted 2030-01-01 literal).
detail: The diff swapped the boundary literal 2030-01-01 for the today+90d template, which always passes the 12-month limit, so the scenario deterministically fails (confirmation, not validation_error) and contradicts the SKILL.md doc in the same diff.
recommended_fix: Restore a dynamic but out-of-range literal (e.g. a {MOVE_IN_DATE_PLUS_13M} template or computed date > today+12 months) and keep the in-past scenario's literal as is.

title: listing-source-tamper still expects a field-listing_source-error span that F4 removed from the SSR — scenario can never pass
evidence: Scenario: `expected_error_fields:` / `  - listing_source` / `tamper_hidden_inputs:` / `  - field: listing_source` / `    inject_value: "blackhat-scraper"`. Harness rule (SKILL.md:206): `validation_error` → `[data-testid="error-summary"]` visible AND each `expected_error_fields:` entry has its `field-{name}-error` span populated`. `grep -rn "field-listing_source\|listing_source-error" server/src/ server/priv/static/` returns zero matches (the view_select_field for listing_source was deleted from work_income.gleam in this diff).
detail: The server still rejects the tampered value, but the error re-render no longer contains any listing_source field or error span, so the scenario's declared expected_error_fields check is unsatisfiable — a deterministic E2E failure introduced by the rework.
recommended_fix: Verify this scenario on the error-summary banner entry alone (drop listing_source from expected_error_fields and assert the summary lists the friendly label), or keep a rendered error target for removed-but-accepted fields.

title: Soak scenario left off the stepper=off rollout — its smoke-iteration click targets a submit button the stepper hides
evidence: Soak scenario: `  - action: click` / `    selector: '[data-testid="submit-application"]'` / `    description: "Submit applicant 1 via the real browser path"`. Stepper (form_stepper.js:390): `s.el.hidden = idx !== i;` — the submit button lives in the review_consent fieldset, hidden until step 8. The diff's own rationale (form-bug-hunt/SKILL.md NAV_URL comment): `the F1 stepper (form_stepper.js) hides sections 2–8 and Playwright refuses fills into hidden sections`. The soak scenario's navigate targets `/apply/<short_code>` with no `stepper=off`.
detail: Every other /apply consumer was taught ?stepper=off in this diff, but the soak workflow (staging-targeted, real-browser smoke iteration) was missed; once this deploys, its Playwright click on the hidden submit button times out and the smoke iteration fails deterministically.
recommended_fix: Append stepper=off when resolving the soak target URL (same case-block pattern as NAV_URL), or drive the stepper's per-section continue buttons in the smoke iteration.

title: listing_source_options is now dead production code kept alive only by its own parity test
evidence: `pub const listing_source_options = [` — grep for `listing_source_options` across server/src and server/test returns only the definition (work_income.gleam:37) and the test (application_handler_test.gleam:905-907: `pub fn listing_source_options_match_validator_whitelist_test() {` / `work_income_section.listing_source_options`). Nothing renders it after this diff.
detail: The comment's rationale (stale cached pages posting the field) is served by the handler's is_valid_listing_source and the DB CHECK, not by this const. The parity test now pins a form-side mirror of a form that no longer exists — drift guard guarding nothing.
recommended_fix: Drop the const and re-point the parity test at the real contract (is_valid_listing_source against the documented whitelist/DB CHECK), or move the accepted set into application_handler.

title: Error summary still links listing_source errors to #field-listing_source, an anchor that no longer exists
evidence: `    "listing_source" -> "Where did you find this listing?"` and `pub fn anchor_for(key: String) -> String {` / `  "field-" <> url_encode_brackets(key)` — but grep shows no `field-listing_source` element renders post-F4. The handler still emits the error (application_handler.gleam:425: `False -> [#("listing_source", "Pick how you found this listing."), ..errors]`). Stepper fallback: `if (!target) return; // unknown anchor — let the browser try`.
detail: On the (admittedly rare) tampered-post path the banner renders a listing_source row whose anchor resolves to nothing — a dead link on the error page, and the stepper's routing silently no-ops. Same removed-field/kept-validation boundary as the scenario break.
recommended_fix: For keys with no rendered field, render the summary row without an anchor link (or map listing_source to the error summary itself) so the banner never points at a missing target.

title: Applicant-facing copy hardcoded in form_stepper.js instead of SSR-owned data attributes (the form.js pattern)
evidence: `  var GATING_MESSAGE = "This one's needed before you continue.";` and `  var REVIEW_HINT_STEPPER =` / `    "Use Back to check any of your answers — nothing is sent until you choose Submit Application.";` — versus form.js:407-408: `var PER_FILE_MESSAGE = section.getAttribute("data-per-file-message");` / `var AGGREGATE_MESSAGE = section.getAttribute("data-aggregate-message");` (SSR owns the copy). SSR hint it overwrites at runtime (review_consent.gleam): `"Have a quick scroll through your answers before submitting."`
detail: The established boundary keeps applicant-facing strings in the SSR copy modules (form_copy.gleam/copy.gleam), passed to JS via data attributes. The stepper embeds two user-facing strings in static JS and creates a second source of truth for the review hint, weakening single-ownership of form copy.
recommended_fix: Render the gating message and stepper review hint as data attributes from the SSR copy modules and have form_stepper.js read them, mirroring form.js's data-per-file-message pattern.
